title: Transient gap-junction blockade makes planarian fragments build heads of other species

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Transient gap-junction blockade makes planarian fragments build heads of other species

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Temporary exposure of planarian fragments to a blocker of electrical synapses (gap junctions) causes them to build head shapes of other planarian species 100–150 million years distant, with no genetic change; Levin interprets this as the bioelectric network navigating to other attractors in morphospace, and the worms later remodel back to normal.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: One example of this plasticity of morphogenetic behavior (expanding on the default genetically encoded repertoire) is the fact that temporary exposure to a blocker of electrical synapses (i.e., an anesthetic) causes planarian fragments to create the heads of other species, with no genetic change required (Emmons-Bell et al. 2015; Sullivan et al. 2016).

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity”. Scope: Planarian flatworms (Girardia dorotocephala and related species), author's lab (Emmons-Bell et al. 2015)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Head geometry and reversion are directly measurable, and published measurements can test the core phenotype. Existing material is less able to establish the attractor interpretation or fully audit genotype and all individual outcomes.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure head-shape landmarks and later remodeling in gap-junction-blocked versus control fragments, then compare treated shapes with reference species while confirming unchanged genotype.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Species-shape similarity and attractor language are partly interpretation-dependent.

Primary raw images and individual-worm measurements may not be deposited.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: An open morphometric study reports canonical variates for more than sixty worms and describes later remodeling, and public divergence times can check the phylogenetic-distance clause. The coordinate file itself is not downloadable, and there is no independent raw archive or sequence check of the altered animals. Shape similarity can therefore be re-examined only in part, and the attractor wording is not separated from a graded wound response.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare landmark Procrustes distances of octanol-treated Girardia dorotocephala regenerates with water-treated controls and with wild-type heads of the named other species, and score whether the same individuals later return to the Girardia shape without a species-diagnostic genotype change. Support would be treated heads falling inside the other species' shape clusters and later leaving them; a continuous rounding that never matches those clusters, or a required genetic change, would weaken the result.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Landmark coordinates are not deposited, so a reanalysis has to be digitized from the published images.

Treated animals were not sequenced, so absence of genetic change is inferred from wild-type parentage.

Octanol is not a gap-junction-specific reagent, and rounded heads can form a continuum rather than discrete species attractors.
